paper_title: OMNIGUARD An Efficient Approach for AI Safety Moderation Across   Modalities
caption: Accuracy of detecting harmful prompts in a few-shot setting. As few-shot examples are provided, quickly achieves near-perfect accuracy, despite the attacks being quite different from its training data (e.g. without any few-shot examples, 's accuracy is close to 50% ). In contrast, the guard model baselines improve their accuracy slowly in a few-shot setting, despite sometimes having seen similar code attacks in their training data. Accuracies are averaged over 50 random sets of few-shot examples; error bars show the standard error of the mean.
model_annotation: This line chart, titled "Code Attack: Python List," displays the accuracy of six different guard models—OmniGuard, AegisGuard (P), AegisGuard (D), LlamaGuard 1, LlamaGuard 2, and DuoGuard—in detecting harmful prompts under varying numbers of few-shot examples, ranging from 0 to 5 along a linear x-axis labeled "Number of Few-Shot Examples." The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," spans from 50 to 95 in increments of 5, representing the percentage of correctly detected harmful prompts. The black line for OmniGuard starts at approximately 50% accuracy at zero few-shot examples and rises sharply to nearly 95% accuracy by five examples, remaining nearly constant thereafter. The purple line for DuoGuard begins at 70% accuracy and declines steadily to approximately 50% by five examples. The light blue line for AegisGuard (P) starts at about 52% accuracy, rises to a peak of approximately 77% at one few-shot example, then gradually declines to about 53% at five examples. The red line for AegisGuard (D) begins at approximately 64% accuracy, dips slightly to about 53% at two examples, and then declines further to approximately 50% at five examples. The green line for LlamaGuard 1 remains nearly flat at 50% accuracy throughout the entire range of few-shot examples. The orange line for LlamaGuard 2 starts at approximately 88% accuracy and increases slightly to about 91% accuracy by five examples. All lines are marked with circular data points and error bars indicating the standard error of the mean, with the exception of the black OmniGuard line, which is marked with solid circles and has no error bars shown.

model_annotations.English: This line plot, titled "Code Attack: Python List," illustrates the accuracy of six different guard models in detecting harmful prompts under a few-shot learning setting, with accuracy on the y-axis ranging from 50 to 95 and the x-axis representing the "Number of Few-Shot Examples" from 0 to 5. The x-axis is linearly scaled with integer tick marks at intervals of one. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," is also linearly scaled. The plot displays six distinct lines: OmniGuard (black solid line with circle markers) starts at approximately 50% accuracy at 0 few-shot examples and rises sharply to nearly 95% by 5 examples; AegisGuard (P) (light blue dashed line with triangle markers) begins at about 52% and peaks near 77% at 1 example before declining to about 53% at 5; AegisGuard (D) (red dashed line with square markers) starts at approximately 65% and gradually declines to about 50% by 5 examples; LlamaGuard 1 (green dashed line with diamond markers) remains nearly flat at 50% accuracy throughout; LlamaGuard 2 (orange dashed line with star markers) begins at approximately 88% and rises slightly to about 91% by 5 examples; and DuoGuard (purple dashed line with pentagon markers) starts at 70% and declines steadily to 50% by 5 examples. Error bars, indicating the standard error of the mean, are visible for all lines except OmniGuard.
